question.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3x+y+3z \\ 2x+y+z \\ x-y+5z\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ k\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}3\cdot (-2)+3+3\cdot k \\ 2\cdot (-2)+3+k \\ -2-3+5\cdot k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-3+3k \\ -1+k \\ -5+5k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3+3k=0 \\ -1+k=0 \\ -5+5k=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to all three of these equations is $k=1.$
